verdict:
THE REVIEWER'S CHALLENGE IS HALF RIGHT, AND THE PRIOR CURATION RECORD WAS HALF WRONG - BUT purity_pct STILL STAYS TBD FOR ALL 259 OLIGOS.

The reviewer was right that regulatory CMC sections exist and are substantive. They were wrong that those sections state purity. The prior record's phrase 'structurally unavailable' was correct about the NUMBER and wrong about the CHARACTERISATION, which it should never have lumped in with it.

WHAT THE CHALLENGE CORRECTLY PREDICTED. EMA EPARs do carry a Quality aspects section with Active Substance manufacture, characterisation and specification, and it is rich. Twelve EPARs were downloaded and read in full (~3.9 MB of text, unredacted prose). From them this pass recovered, for 11 of the 14 named compounds: the exact analytical method behind every purity and impurity test (IP-HPLC-UV-MS for the Ionis MOE gapmers; AX-HPLC plus IPRP-HPLC orthogonal pairs for the Alnylam/Novartis siRNAs; SE-HPLC for duplex state; LC-UV/MS for imetelstat; LC-UV-MS for tofersen); the full specification parameter list; the impurity taxonomy including the N-1 and N+1 species and their formation mechanisms, verbatim; explicit full-length-product attributes (nusinersen's purity test is literally named 'purity (Full Length n)', inotersen's specification carries 'full length product content', imetelstat's acronym table defines FLP, 12mers and 14mers); every counter-ion and salt form with molecular formula and mass; and a complete diastereomer statement for every compound. That last category alone repaid the pass: it CONFIRMED dataset ps_count for inotersen, volanesorsen, mipomersen, olezarsen (2^19 each), nusinersen (2^17) and inclisiran (6 PS); it RECOVERED ps_count for eplontersen (13) and vutrisiran (6), both TBD in the dataset; it RECOVERED imetelstat's sequence, TAGGGTTAGACAA, also TBD; and it CONTRADICTED the dataset on tofersen, which oligos.csv records as full_PS with ps_count=19 but which the Qalsody EPAR states is a MIXED backbone of 15 phosphorothioates and 4 phosphate diesters - corroborated three ways by the molecular formula C230H317N72O123P19S15, by '2^15 (i.e. 32,768) diastereoisomers', and by the published linkage-by-linkage shorthand, which also yields a full modification_map for a compound where that field is TBD. Eleven of fourteen named compounds now have a documented purity METHOD where they previously had 'TBD', and two have corrected or newly recovered backbone chemistry.

WHAT THE CHALLENGE GOT WRONG. Not one numeric drug-substance purity value exists in any of these documents. Two exhaustive regex sweeps across the combined EMA + FDA corpus - one for any purity/assay/FLP term within 25 characters of a two-digit percentage or an NLT/NMT/>= qualifier, one for any 80-99.x% figure within 70 characters of purity, impurity, full, area, assay, content, FLP, duplex or strand - returned ZERO hits. The EPARs state that limits exist, that they were justified, and repeatedly that they were TIGHTENED during the procedure, and then never give them. The FDA side is worse, not better: the nusinersen chemistry review carries the stamp '136 Page(s) has been Withheld in Full as b4 (CCI/TS)'; defibrotide's withholds 125 pages; pegaptanib's withholds 56 and then 46; the imetelstat review releases 24 of 156 pages and the withheld portion is exactly the section its own table of contents calls 'Characterization of Drug Substance and Impurities'; fomivirsen's 1998 review has its specification pages physically removed and the remainder obscured with hand-applied whiteout; and the surviving inline text is punctuated by (b)(4) at precisely the load-bearing points - 'Purity is determined [REDACTED]', 'a limit of not less than (NLT) [REDACTED] mL', 'The drug substance specification include the following test attributes: [WHITED OUT]'. The single most quotable sentence in the pegaptanib review is the one that stops mid-thought where the answer should be.

WHY THIS IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A SEARCH FAILURE. Two independent reasons, both from the regulators themselves. First, acceptance criteria are Confidential Commercial Information: FDA withholds them under FOIA Exemption 4 and EMA simply omits them from the published EPAR, and this is uniform across every product and every year from 1998 to 2025. Second, and more fundamental, there is no class-level standard to fall back on. EMA/BfArM's R. Thuermer told the EMA RNA-based medicines conference on 2 February 2023 (slide 8) that 'In contrast to synthetic peptides no purity limits are stated in the Ph. Eur. Monograph Substances for pharmaceutical use for synthetic oligonucleotides', and the public consultation on the proposed EU oligonucleotide guideline returned the key message (slide 10) to 'Discourage from trying to establish generic purity limits - these are too dependent on chemistry, sequence (even within the same chemistry) and method'. There is no compendial number to find because the field has deliberately declined to set one, and each product's number is a company-specific trade secret. Note also that where oligonucleotide purity does appear as a percentage in these documents it is a TRAP: the Tryngolza EPAR's '81.7%' is the fraction of fully conjugated full-length ASO in MOUSE PLASMA one hour post-dose on day 42, measured by a non-validated in-house method - in vivo biotransformation, not analytical purity. It was found, checked, and rejected under hard rules 1 and 3 rather than transcribed.

THE ONE QUANTITATIVE COMPOSITION LIMIT FOUND ANYWHERE, and it is instructive: defibrotide's EPAR states 'mean oligonucleotide length is 50 bases with a mean molecular weight of 17 +/- 4 kDa, and at least 40% being >12 kDa'. That is a real published specification - and it exists precisely because defibrotide is a polydisperse porcine DNA extract for which no conventional purity assay is possible, so the molecular-weight distribution IS the specification. It is recorded in notes, not in purity_pct, because it is a size-distribution criterion and not a purity percentage. Defibrotide is also, like fomivirsen and pegaptanib, NOT ACTUALLY IN THIS DATASET - the task named 14 compounds 'in this dataset' but only 11 resolve against oligos.csv, which is logged as its own ledger item.

BOTTOM LINE. Concede the number, reject the generalisation. purity_pct = TBD is correct and should stay, and the reason should be upgraded in the curation record from the vague 'structurally unavailable' to the specific and defensible: numeric purity acceptance criteria are withheld as confidential commercial information by both FDA (Exemption 4, with page-count stamps citable per product) and EMA, and no compendial purity limit exists for synthetic oligonucleotides per the Ph. Eur. and the EMA's own 2023 position. But purity_METHOD, characterization_source, the counter-ion and salt form, the molecular formula, the impurity taxonomy, the diastereomer count and - for tofersen and eplontersen - the positional modification map are all recoverable, were recovered here, and were NOT structurally unavailable. The prior record conflated the two. Zero purity values were invented; 11 purity methods, 11 diastereomer statements, 11 salt/counter-ion records, 2 corrected or recovered backbone chemistries, 1 recovered sequence and 1 full positional modification map were gained.
